subject: swampTroll
pitch:
Category: Monster.
Subject: swamp troll with tusks, mohawk and bone fetishes.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.
reasoning:
I'm planning a compact swamp troll design—hunched jungle troll with long arms, tusks, mohawk, and bone fetishes—while sticking to reliable helper functions like joint, chain, sweep, and part to keep the build stable.

I'm laying out the skeleton for the troll: hips at the base, a spine chain curving upward and forward through 1.05-1.75m height, then a neck chain extending to a head joint near 1.98m, using catmull-rom paths with named joints for spine1/spine2/chest and neck1/neck2/head, each parented to the previous chain's tip. I'm also planning to apply paint with mottled, countershaded coloring for the skin.

For the body I'm sweeping the spine chain with an elliptical radius function to form the torso, widening from hips to chest for a hunched, broad-shouldered look, and defining the skin as a green-teal countershaded mottle for a swampy troll appearance.

Now I'm placing the head: computing a world-space head center position, attaching a scaled sphere to the head bone for the skull, adding a heavy brow shape, and setting up a separate jaw piece on its own joint.

Still defining more facial features...

Then I'm adding ears as backward-up spikes from the head sides, and a mohawk crest of alternating red/crimson spikes running from forehead to nape, leaning back along the neck, all attached to the head bone.

Now I'm setting up long ape-like arms, chaining shoulder, elbow, and hand joints parented to the chest, bending the elbows backward, with tapered limb radii and fist spheres capping the hands.

Adding shoulder spikes and a leather mantle with bone fetishes, then working out the legs: hip-to-foot IK with two segments bending the knee forward digitigrade-style, plus a boxy foot with claw spikes positioned to rest at ground level.

Now I'm figuring out the loincloth as an extruded trapezoid flap hanging from the hips front and back, with a belt to finish the pelvis area.

Checking the torus fits against the torso radius at that height, it seems fine since the major radius slightly exceeds the belly width. Now I'm thinking about adding bone fetish details—a necklace of small bone capsules and a skull made from a sphere and jaw box, hanging on the chest, trying to figure out the right surface point and normal direction to anchor them using a ray cast from in front of the torso.

Thinking I should tilt the bone studs to lie tangent along the necklace curve rather than stick straight out, and I'm adding a central skull pendant made from a scaled sphere, jaw box, and black eye sockets hanging from a string. I'm also planning hip fetish bundles with bones and feathers hanging from the belt.

I'll add tribal war-paint stripes across the cheeks using position-based masking tied to facial coordinates, plus glowing yellow eyes with small black pupils set forward. For the rig, I'm planning joint names including a jaw role and three claw-spike fingers per hand.

Simplifying the hands to plain rods spread from the fist pointing down-forward, skipping extra finger joints for cost reasons, and adding clawed toes on the feet. I'm placing a hunched back hump as a scaled sphere on the upper back near the shoulder line, keeping the color count manageable, then moving into writing the actual helper functions for spheres and other shapes.

Writing torso sweep code...

Now I'm working out the limb mounting logic: shoulders and hips get joints parented to the spine, with chains for arms and legs sharing a bend direction (knee/elbow forward), and computing reach lengths like shoulder-to-hand distance for the arm.

For the spikes, I'm setting up a helper that draws each spike as a cone from a base point to a tip point along a bone, then using that to build the mohawk by interpolating a curved path of points down the skull toward the neck, shaping the bump height and z-depth with power curves.

I'm giving each spike a root-to-tip color gradient alternating between red and orange tones, then planning small side ear spikes with a gold ring earring, a skull pendant, and a fetish bundle hanging from the hip on the belt.

Adding hanging feather cards with a teal leaf-shaped texture tipped in red, framed and oriented on bone hip points, while deciding to skip extra weapons and totems per the brief and focusing only on tusks, mohawk, and fetishes. I'm now setting up the imports needed from the builder kit for frames, limbs, curves, shading, and gradients.

I'm placing the jaw joint and lower jaw geometry using scaled sphere parts, checking ground contact and overall height proportions from feet to mohawk tip, and positioning the tusk bases relative to the jaw.

Now I'm working out the snout, nose spike, brow ridge, and eye placements relative to skull radius, making sure the eyes sit slightly embedded in the face rather than floating outside it.

Positioning the skull sphere, then generating finger and claw geometry off the hand joint positions, and setting up the material colors for bone, red, and leather tones.

Now I'm defining the loincloth as an extruded shape positioned against the hip area with a stripe pattern, working out the outline points so the extrusion stays non-self-intersecting.

Now I'm adding a mirrored flap at the back, then moving on to coding the necklace loop geometry.
